text:
ana: Heads-up — we started seeing a spike in structured-output validation rejections on route /v1/generate-tool today after the midnight rollout. Rejection rate ~6% in the last hour.
kevin: Oh neat, any pattern in the payload shape?
ana: Noticed tool responses missing the `result.items` array sometimes, returning `result` as a string instead. Likely a model variant fallback returning legacy shape.
kevin: Can you paste an example error from validation?
ana: Sure:
```
{"error":"schema_validation","path":"response.result.items","expected":"array","received":"string","request_id":"req_3fa2"}
```
sam: That's the old 1.1 tool format leaking through. Our routing policy should've prevented fallback to the legacy handler. Did autoscaler trigger a cheaper model?
ana: Yes, routing logs show requests routed to `text-tool-legacy-q8` during a short capacity pressure window. Policy had `allow_backfill: true` for low-priority routes.
kevin: We intentionally permitted backfill to avoid timeouts, but schema regressions are bad. Two questions: (1) should the API accept variant shapes and run a shim? (2) should console flag these as errors/alerts?
nora: I vote we reject at the API layer (422) and surface counts in console. If we silently coerce, app devs will be surprised by subtle type changes.
sam: Rejection is better for correctness, but we must differentiate between transient backfills vs real model regression. Add a per-route metric: `structured_schema_rejects{route, model_variant}` and a short window alert (>=1% for 15m).
ana: Agreed. We currently emit `schema_reject` only to logs. Need telemetry pipeline to export to metrics (Prometheus) and to Console dashboards.
kevin: Console UX: add a small widget on route page showing `Schema rejects` with sample failing payloads (redact PII) and top offending model variants. Also let customers toggle `strict_schema: on|warn|off` per route.
ops-bot: Deployed canary policy change detected: route /v1/generate-tool reduced `allow_backfill` to false at 1792222200 by kevin.
kevin: That was a quick follow-up — but some of the requests during the window already failed. How do we backfill customers affected?
nora: We should surface a per-customer row in console: #failed_requests, first_failure_ts, sample_error, rollout-version that served them. Add an exportable CSV for support teams.
sam: Implementation notes: 1) validation lib already returns structured error objects — we need a mapping function to increment a statsd counter per `route|variant|error_code`. 2) Collector must batch these and expose to prometheus. 3) Console needs API to query sample errors by route with rate-limited retrieval.
kevin: Regarding API status codes: prefer 422 for schema validation (client-visible contract broken), 500 for runtime failures. Also include `x-schema-error: true` header and `schema_error_code` in response body.
nana: Small example response idea:
```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error":"schema_validation_failed",
  "schema_error_code":"missing_array_result",
  "request_id":"req_3fa2",
  "hint":"response.result.items expected array; got string. If you recently changed model variant, pin to a fixed variant or enable strict_schema=off."
}
```
kevin: Love the hint field. Add `model_variant` and `served_by` metadata when available.
nora: Who owns the telemetry work? Infra-telemetry + Eng-Platform. Sam can lead the metrics mapping, Ana will do Console UI.
sam: I'll put up a small PR to increment `schema_rejects` counters and emit `sample_error_event` to the log-forwarder with `redact=true`.
ana: For console UI, we should show a timeline and offer quick rollback to previous rollout version from the route page. Also provide a one-click pin: `pin_to_variant` to avoid backfill.
kevin: Ops playbook draft: when >1% rejects for 15m -> create incident postmortem stub, tag `schema-regression`, automatic rollback candidate listing.
ana: One more ask — add a toggle in the rollout UX: `prevent_variant_backfill_if_schema_mismatch` (default true). That prevents routing to variants that fail validate against the route's schema.
sam: Implementation caveat: validation costs CPU; we should sample validation at 100% for the failing window and 5% otherwise. Or run validation in parallel worker that doesn't block critical path when sampling is off.
kevin: Good point. Start with 100% for suspect windows. We'll iterate.
nana: I'll create a short doc and a Console mock for the widget. Linking the draft here: https://redwood.internal/links/rdw-538
kevin: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow quick standup to prioritize infra tickets. :thumbsup:
